description: Braspace is a Brazilian team from Uberlândia passionate about space exploration, AI, and innovation. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're tackling the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, combining software engineering, geospatial data, AI, and interactive visualization to explore lunar landing opportunities. We welcome curious, collaborative minds skilled in Python, AI/ML, GIS, data science, astronomy, UX/UI, and 3D visualization. Let's build the future of lunar exploration together!
summary: At the Moon’s south pole, a ridge can determine when a surface mission receives sunlight and when it can see Earth. MoonProof makes those windows visible. Our educational browser demo uses NASA lunar elevation data and JPL ephemerides to show a 72-hour example at Connecting Ridge. Explore when the Sun and Earth rise above the local terrain horizon, then test how a later arrival changes a simplified scenario. The demo shows the sources and assumptions behind the results. Independent numerical validation is pending.
details:
Why the horizon matters

At the lunar south pole, the Sun stays low in the sky. Nearby terrain casts shadows and can also block a direct line of sight to Earth. MoonProof shows both conditions on one timeline so readers can see when the windows overlap.

Try the demonstration

Open the Connecting Ridge example and inspect the hourly Sun and Earth positions relative to the terrain horizon. Try a later arrival in the recovery scenario and compare the resulting trade-offs. In class, ask students to find an hour with sunlight but no direct view of Earth.

How we produced the example

We derived the local terrain horizon from the NASA LRO/LOLA south polar elevation model at 80 m per pixel. JPL/NAIF SPICE kernels give the geometric directions to the Sun and Earth centers. For each hour, we compare each elevation with the terrain horizon at its azimuth. The public demo displays the precomputed 72-hour example and its provenance.

How to interpret the results

Geometric Earth visibility is one input to a radio link analysis. Solar exposure is one input to spacecraft power analysis. Terrain resolution, observer height and hourly sampling affect the modeled windows. Independent reference checks and an uncertainty budget are pending. The simulation is an educational prototype.

AI assistance

Generative AI assisted ideation, research, coding, debugging and editing. The team is responsible for reviewing the implementation, sources and claims.
